newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican spot peso closes weaker, rates, jitters.
newsitem.headline: Mexican spot peso closes weaker, rates, jitters.

text.p: The Mexican peso lost ground it had gained in early trading on Tuesday due to local dollar demand to cover short positions, the rebound in U.S. long bond rates and political uncertainty, traders said.
"The peso slid back a little before the close following demand from banks to cover their (short) dollar positions...supposedly because of long bond rates," a trader said.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yield was 7.13 percent as the peso market was closing in Mexico, compared to an early low of 7.06 percent.
The 48-hour spot peso closed 0.65 of a centavo weaker at 7.5500/7.5550 per dollar, while 24-hour contracts closed 1.05 centavos weaker at 7.5480/7.5530 per dollar.

Other traders put the demand for dollars by some foreign investors down to fears of a possible outbreak of political violence on Mexico's Independance Day, on September 16, when local financial markets will be closed.
"Some foreigners covered positions in advance of the long weekend as they fear that an armed group may cause problems for the Independence Day celebrations," a currency trader said.
The same-day peso closed earlier 0.5 of a centavo firmer 7.5300/7.5330 per dollar.
Traders estimated that the peso may weaken against the dollar on Wednesday, as domestic interest rates are expected to fall by about 100 basis points at Tuesday evening's primary auction.
